0.content:
Bamoun, called the "Bearer of Bloodshed", was the previous leader of the Temple of Silence and Sethos's adoptive grandfather. Sethos remembers him not as a stern leader but as a kind, patient man who took him camping, hunting and exploring in the desert and read with him by lamplight. He offered Sethos as a vessel for a Ba fragment and paid Cyno's parents for their son. Old, half-blind and dying, he and Sethos planned Cyrus's return. He lived just long enough to watch the Rite of Duels and see Hermanubis's light in Cyno, then died in his chair. Sethos knelt before him and later mourned at his tomb.

Sethos sensed that Bamoun's distaste for Cyrus hid friendship: Bamoun gave him a fine polearm Cyrus had left behind. Grandfather and grandson came to an unspoken understanding that one day they would stand together "at the crossroads of history", and that Bamoun's last sacrifice would be himself. Temple members say the two were very close and must have agreed on the reconciliation long ago.

1.content:
The General Mahamatra is Sethos's first friend and his opposite. Both were childhood vessels at the Temple; the fragments erased Cyno's memory of the Temple almost entirely and took some of Sethos's memories of people. They met again as opponents in 4.6: Sethos pretended never to have seen him, and Cyno then beat him in the Rite of Duels and took his fragment. Cyno refused the leadership and gave it to Sethos, saying the experience had made them friends and the two institutions partners. Sethos calls him "bro", a worthy heir of Hermanubis who reveres wisdom, and finds the way he talks hilarious.

Cyno respects Sethos's sense of responsibility, his courage and his skill as a warrior, but complains that Sethos is always "busy" whenever Genius Invokation comes up. Sethos lives in Sumeru City partly because, unlike the famous Cyno, he wanted an unremarkable life. Cyno reflected that Sethos was asking the same questions he once had (who am I, why this power, what to fight for) and would find his answers.

2.comment: Sethos: Oathkeeper and the Rite of Duels
2.content:
Cyno's Story Quest Act II (4.6). Sethos manipulated the scholar Urraca into carrying a vague threat to Cyrus, who recognised the Temple's emblem and went into the desert. Sethos met Cyno's party at an oasis, raised the hidden Temple from the sand, and later took charge when Bamoun collapsed. The Rite of Duels, said to recreate Hermanubis's sparring with Tulaytullah's people, set three challengers against the Temple. Sethos demanded that both fragments go to the winner. The Traveler and Tighnari won the first bouts against Temple guardians; Cyno beat Sethos in the third. Sethos yielded and passed his fragment to Cyno.

Before the final bout Sethos declared his titles and the Temple's long faithfulness, then admitted the faith had held them back. He had seen the city and believed times had changed, and asked Cyno to show him who he could become. Afterwards he granted access to the Temple's archives to anyone Cyno and Nahida deem worthy, with a warning to choose carefully, and told Tighnari the Tighnarians' shared history with Hermanubis.

3.content:
An ancient order founded by Hermanubis after King Deshret's death to keep knowledge that should not reach the world. It fled Tulaytullah after betrayal, spent time in the rainforest working with the Akademiya, left again out of mistrust, and finally settled in a hidden underground temple near Thamud Oasis. The Akademiya's "Temple of Silence" office is only a hollow front. Sethos now leads the real one.

Most members stay at the base researching and tending ancient technology, and occasionally investigate newly found ruins; Sethos never misses those trips. Desert-dwellers and scholars of Deshret's civilization know the name. In 6.6 the Temple hosted the evacuated scholars and its records led the search for a new power source for the Akasha.

4.comment: Sethos: Hermanubis and the Ba Fragments
4.content:
Hermanubis, a Tighnarian warrior who served King Deshret and later founded the Temple, broke his being into fragments to save the Temple from Gurabad's army. The Temple held two Ba fragments; only children could bear them. Sethos and Cyno each received one, and Sethos lost some memories of people as a result. Sethos gave his to Cyno after the duel, so Cyno now holds both.

Sethos told Cyno that each fragment stands for something different, such as might or glory. He still speaks of sharing a connection to Hermanubis with Cyno (6.1, limited event). He calls whether surviving that power was a blessing or a curse an open question, but says it gave him a higher purpose.

5.content:
After the duel, Tighnari wrote inviting Sethos to Gandharva Ville to meet Cyno's friends. Sethos found out only later that Tighnari copes badly with desert heat, and admires how well he fought anyway. Sethos loves Tighnari's stories about the forest and its lost visitors, goes with Cyno to mooch meals, shows off his tent-pitching and competes with Collei at making camp, which leaves her feeling redundant. He is horrified that Tighnari grills without seasoning.

In the 6.1 event (limited), Sethos, Cyno and Tighnari explored ruins as a trio, swapping jokes about Cyno's puns and a commemorative slab of their own.

6.content: Cyrus, Cyno's mentor and a former Spantamad sage, was rescued in the desert by Bamoun and worked with him on the Ba fragment experiment, then left with Cyno. Sethos framed his recall as a debt coming due and told him it was too late for persuasion because he had betrayed Bamoun. Cyrus in turn said Sethos had the courage and judgment of a young Bamoun. After the funeral Sethos sent the others to find Cyrus in Bamoun's room, suspecting the old man had many fond memories there, and joked that all of them had been pawns in his grandfather's plan.

7.content: Sethos first asked him outright whether he was "Hat Guy", and has wanted a closer look at the hat ever since. Their exchange at the Akademiya's side gate, each saying the other has a more important role than he lets on, is the closest either comes to admitting anything. The Wanderer calls him "that green-eyed desert guy" and insists they have barely spoken. In 6.6 they formed the fast-moving supply team with Cyno; Sethos teased that the job suited the fleet-footed.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
8.content: When Irminsul malfunctioned and Nahida collapsed, Sumeru evacuated to Caravan Ribat. Sethos proposed the Temple of Silence as the place to search King Deshret's records for a substitute for the Gnosis that powered the Akasha. The Temple became the base, and the search led to Aaru. Sethos introduced himself to the freed Pillars and told them they could help make history. He then helped Cyno and the Wanderer salvage Primal Constructs in the Mausoleum for terminals (he had never had an Akasha Terminal himself). During the operation he stood with Heryshaf at King Deshret's throne for the chant. Afterwards he parted with Dehya and Candace at Caravan Ribat, inviting them to the Temple.

9.comment: Sethos: Thoth, Heryshaf and the Seven Pillars
9.content: Temple records name the Goat King Heryshaf (Minister of Ministers), Sobek the Crocodile King (Captain of Captains) and Thoth the Ibis King (Scribe of Scribes, inventor of the desert script) as Hermanubis's fellow Pillars. Sethos once doubted Aaru, "the far side of Eternity", existed; Thoth's tale and the 6.6 crisis proved it. After the crisis Thoth and Heryshaf chose to stay at the Temple, though they refused to have their statues moved in out of respect for Hermanubis; Nahida left Sethos to settle the arrangement. Sethos quotes Heryshaf's saying that a god without his people ceases to exist.

10.content: Dehya, the Flame-Mane, met him in the desert as a down-to-earth man who once shared his drinking water with her troubled mercenaries, and only recently learned of his Temple role; he rates her the second-best guide in the Great Red Sand. Candace, Guardian of Aaru Village, calls him a proud son of Deshret, hosted him, and introduced him to villagers as a "traveler" from the heart of the desert. He took that word to Bamoun's tomb: now he has seen more places than his grandfather ever did. After the 6.6 crisis the three discussed belief, gods and friendship on the road home.

11.content: Nefer, a desert-born intel broker from Nod-Krai, came to Sumeru with Nicole during the 6.6 crisis and helped free the Pillars. Sethos approached her openly, saying he is easier to talk to than Cyno and more streetwise than Tighnari, and invited her to put down her burdens and return home. She noticed he was luring her in; he called it an invitation and wanted her as an asset, mentioning that the power they both hold first belonged to the same organization (unexplained in canon). She called him a more interesting heir to Bamoun than expected.

12.comment: Sethos: The Ordinary Life in Sumeru City
12.content: In the city nobody can remember when he arrived, yet everyone thinks he is an old friend. He runs errands for students and the elderly, takes gifts in return, helps a Treasures Street shopkeeper, guides researchers into the desert and assists caravans. At Lambad's Tavern he tells stories of desert crossings. Once, to a table of drunk friends, he described a hero with a golden key to a lost treasure, and was delighted when the owner said such a person could not be that young. Dehya, hearing the tale, guessed the truth without saying it. A researcher once urged him to sit the Akademiya entrance exam; he said he would consider it.
